results.bash53_output: `kill -n 0 $$; echo rc=$?` -> rc=0, no stderr. `sleep 30 & p=$!; kill -n 15 $p; echo rc=$?; wait $p; echo wrc=$?` -> `rc=0` / `wrc=143` (child actually got SIGTERM). `kill -n bogus $$` -> rc=1 `kill: bogus: invalid signal specification`.
results.psh_output: `kill -n 0 $$; echo rc=$?` -> rc=1, stderr `psh: line 1: kill: invalid signal name: n`. `sleep 30 & p=$!; kill -n 15 $p; echo rc=$?; wait $p; echo wrc=$?` -> `rc=1` / `wrc=0` with the same stderr (signal never delivered; `wait` blocked until `sleep 30` exited normally). `kill -n bogus $$` -> rc=1 `psh: line 1: kill: invalid signal name: n` (the `-n` itself is parsed as signal NAME `n`; `bogus` never inspected).
